transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2025-08-20
Time: 16:00 UTC
Duration: 47 minutes
Attendees: Jordan Lee (Redwood AE), Maya Patel (Redwood SE), Claire Wong (Redwood CSM), Samir Khan (Lumenix Head of ML), Priya Menon (CTO), Diego Alvarez (SRE), Ana Torres (Product)

[00:00] Jordan: hey everyone thanks for joining the QBR, uh real quick agenda — usage/costs, reliability incidents, roadmap items that matter to Lumenix, and next steps. Claire you want to add?
[00:15] Claire: just want to make sure we cover the pilot asks and renewal timeline.
[00:21] Samir: yep that's key, we want to see cost improvements and baseline perf before committing to dedicated.
[00:32] Maya: cool, i'll jump in on the perf slides — quick note, we pulled the last 90 days of metrics, included token-level cost, P95/P99 latencies and KV cache hit rates.
[00:44] Priya: thanks, we've had a spike in inference spend last quarter, curious where it's coming from.
[00:51] Jordan: looking at your usage there were two big drivers: backend batch jobs that scaled up during demos and a recent change in prompt length for your chat flows. Those bumped avg tokens per request by about 35%.
[01:07] Diego: that matches what we saw — our ops auto-scale config let a burst through, we were surprised by the cost impact.
[01:13] Maya: on the latency side P95 is holding around 220ms for the hosted endpoints you use, P99 was around 720ms on peak days, and tail latency correlated with cold KV cache misses. The KV cache hit rate for the last 30 days was ~62% on your most used routes, which is good but room to improve.
[01:36] Samir: ok 720ms P99 is... workable but our goal is sub-500ms for user-facing flows. Is that realistic without Dedicated?
[01:43] Maya: depends — with dedicated capacity you get predictable throughput and lower queuing; our benchmarks show similar models hitting P99 ~300-400ms on Dedicated with your seq lengths. On hosted we can optimize batching and prefix caching too but variability remains.
[02:02] Jordan: financially there's a tradeoff — Dedicated has a commit but reduces per-token price, and avoids noisy neighbor effects. We put a rough cost model in the deck.
[02:11] Priya: can you re-send that cost model? we want to run the numbers with our finance team.
[02:15] Claire: yes will attach post-call. Jordan will share updated pricing including a 12-month committed option.
[02:23] [03:00] Maya: small note on quantization — for Lumenix workload we recommended per earlier evals 4-bit quantized variant for the encoder-heavy model. That typically reduces memory footprint and token cost by ~25% with little quality regression on short prompts, though longer context can show slight diffs.
[03:18] Samir: we did some internal evals and saw a mild drop on edge-case prompts — could we run a pilot with 5-6 prompt sets?
[03:25] Maya: absolutely, we'll run the quantized pilot and tie quality monitoring to your eval set; Claire will coordinate.
[03:32] Diego: SRE question — during the May incident we saw 3 partial outages, the incident report mentions fallback routing but we need more detail on root cause and remediation.
[03:42] Jordan: right, those were capacity pressure events in a single region, autoscale didn't bring enough burst capacity fast enough, and the fallback to a larger-latency model triggered. We surfaced a postmortem in the incident log but i'll have Maya export the timeline and full traces.
[03:58] Maya: yes i'll share traces and the CSV of requests that hit fallbacks. Also, we recommended configuring multi-region routing for critical routes to avoid single-region capacity pressure.
[04:12] Priya: what's the work required on our side for multi-region? VPC peering or just route config?
[04:18] Maya: for Private deployments you'd need network setup; for Hosted it's mostly config and we handle routing. For your Dedicated evaluation it's doable with limited networking changes — we'll scope it.
[04:30] Samir: one more on security — our auditors asked about SAML SSO and key management timeline. We need SOC2 plus KMS integration details.
[04:40] Claire: we have a SOC2 report and KMS integration guide, i'll share both. We support customer-managed keys via AWS KMS and HSM options for Private deployments.
[04:51] Ana: can you also include audit log retention options — compliance needs 2-year retention.
[04:55] Claire: noted, will include retention matrix.
[05:02] [05:30] Jordan: quick recap on roadmap items that impact you: 1) improved batching heuristics to lower latency/cost for mixed small/large requests (Q3 release), 2) smarter KV pre-warming to improve cache hit rates (Q4), 3) expanded quantization profiles & evaluation harness (Q3-Q4), and 4) rollout of per-route cost alerts in Console (Q3).
[05:30] Priya: the KV pre-warming — can we tune pre-warm for our high priority routes?
[05:36] Maya: yes, we'll expose a per-route pre-warm config in the Console alpha; we'll include Lumenix as an early adopter for that feature.
[05:44] Diego: about cost alerts, can they trigger a webhook to our slack/ops tool?
[05:48] Jordan: yes, webhooks and email are supported; we'll show config in the demo.
[05:55] Samir: for the pilot scope on quantized models, what success criteria are we using?
[06:00] Maya: suggested success criteria: <=5% degradation on your eval prompts, P95 < 300ms on Dedicated pilot, and >=80% KV cache hit after pre-warm tuning.
[06:12] Samir: sounds fair.
[06:16] [06:30] Jordan: ok next steps — i'll send the pricing and commit options, Maya will share logs and traces, Claire will share SOC2 and KMS docs and create workshop invite. We aim to reconvene after the pilot results.
[06:45] Priya: timeline wise we want pilot started by mid-September to align with our internal Q4 planning.
[06:51] Jordan: noted — we'll target pilot kickoff 2025-09-15.
[06:58] Ana: quick note, can you include a simple runbook for how to switch routes to Dedicated in the event of a sudden traffic spike?
[07:04] Maya: yes short runbook and a one-click route failover doc we'll include.
[07:11] Speaker 1: (unclear) also ask about model version pinning, do we get automatic rollbacks?
[07:16] Maya: you can pin model versions per route and we support canary rollouts and automatic fallback to pinned stable versions on regressions. We'll include the rollout docs.
[07:25] [07:40] Jordan: any other blockers?
[07:43] Priya: just the finance approval once we see dedicated pricing.
[07:46] Samir: and we'll finalize the eval prompt set this week.
[07:50] Jordan: great, thanks everyone. we'll follow up with the artifacts: pricing deck, incident traces, SOC2 & KMS docs, and workshop invite.
[07:58] Claire: thanks all, see you next time.

End of transcript.
